name: RoboNet: Large-Scale Multi-Robot Learning Dataset
description: RoboNet is a landmark multi-robot, multi-domain learning dataset consisting of 162,000 robotic manipulation trajectories spanning roughly 15 million video frames collected across 7 distinct robotic arm platforms operating in unconstrained tabletop environments. Developed collaboratively across UC Berkeley, University of Pennsylvania, and Stanford University, RoboNet was designed to study video prediction, self-supervised visual foresight, and multi-robot policy transfer. Each trajectory contains multi-view RGB video recordings, commanded end-effector actions, and camera calibration parameters.

provenance.collection_method: Autonomous interaction data collection across 7 physical robot platforms (Sawyer, Baxter, Franka Emika Panda, Kuka iiwa, Universal Robots UR3/UR5, and Fetch) interacting with cluttered tables.
provenance.curation_notes: Incorporates multiple camera view angles, gripper orientations, and randomized tabletop object interactions.
